title: Teluni Implementation Plan
html:
Project human actions · Project derivation · Validation · Documentation index

Purpose and baseline

This is Teluni's living execution plan and the current plan for this repository. It tracks product and repository work; the README, current policies, and accepted ADRs govern implementation.

Teluni was initialized on 2026-10-17 from Orion commit 53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea of https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion. The project manifest records that immutable initialization commit and the Orion baseline currently integrated. At initialization, the repository contained the foundation's architecture, policies, ADRs, tooling, validation gate, CI, generated references and Living Documentation Portal, with no product modules. Results recorded for the Orion repository are not results for this repository until they pass in this checkout and in this repository's CI.

Maintaining this plan

Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain this plan and the project human actions within the user's authorized scope.

  1. Before implementation, inspect actual repository state, the relevant task, its prerequisites, governing policy, and linked human actions. Do not treat a planned capability or unchecked action as available.
  2. Mark a task in progress when work actually starts. Update statuses when evidence, scope, dependencies, or blockers change, and before each handoff or completion report.
  3. Allocate stable task IDs as PJ-NN; never reuse or renumber them. Add finer tasks when needed; do not hide unfinished subtasks inside a completed row.
  4. Record concise evidence in the task row: implementation paths, validation commands and results, review references, or a linked decision. Record evidence produced for this repository—local validation, this repository's CI runs, and this repository's external settings. Do not store secret values or sensitive output.
  5. A task becomes completed only when its deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence. A partial implementation or an unavailable required check is not completion.
  6. When human intervention is necessary, add or update a project human action, link it from the affected task, mark that task blocked, and tell the user what is needed. Continue independent authorized work where possible.
  7. A future prerequisite is pending, not automatically blocked.
  8. When scope or sequencing changes, use changed, explain why and what replaces the work, and link supporting decisions. Do not delete unresolved obligations to make the plan look complete.
  9. Update command availability, current documentation, generated artifacts, and the human actions in the same coherent change where applicable. Do not change ADR status merely to record implementation progress.
Status Meaning
pending Not started; includes conditional work whose trigger has not occurred.
in progress Work has started and is incomplete.
completed Applicable deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence.
blocked The identified work cannot proceed without a recorded dependency, decision, access, or correction.
changed Scope, applicability, or sequencing was explicitly revised; reason and replacement or disposition are recorded.

Constraints throughout implementation

  • Retain the accepted stack recorded in the technology map; incompatibilities require explicit resolution rather than silent substitution.
  • Add product capabilities as API modules and web modules composed in apps/api/src/modules.ts and apps/web/src/modules.tsx; Orion's reference implementation shows a complete example.
  • Deliver tests, security controls, telemetry, and documentation with the behavior they protect.
  • Keep generated artifacts reproducible and subordinate to canonical sources. Reviewed SQL migrations follow their separate release-history rules.
  • Require non-mutating pnpm validate for substantial changes, using the same capabilities locally and in CI.
  • Adopt newer Orion revisions only through the reviewed upgrade workflow.

Member administration (2026-10-18): strongly authenticated company administrators page through memberships with presentation names/emails from each person's last verified sign-in, and suspend, reactivate or terminally remove a membership in that company only, with expected versions and one audit event each. Writers lock the company row and then the memberships in ID order and recheck the actor's current administrator grant; the responsible administrator and the last active administrator are protected, and restoring an administrator requires the responsible administrator with strong authentication no older than five minutes. The panel confirms changes with the observed version, reloads after conflicts or unknown outcomes and offers recent re-authentication. Frozen install and full local pnpm validate passed: 110 API tests, 67 web unit tests, 17 browser component tests and 24 E2E journeys; a sign-in race in the journeys (clicking the header link before the page prompt rendered) was fixed and two further full E2E runs passed. Role administration and responsibility transfer (2026-10-18): administrators add standard-role grants over the whole company or explicit active branches with an optional non-renewing expiry, and revoke them; only the responsible administrator with five-minute strong authentication grants administration, and revocation keeps the responsible and last active administrators. The responsible administrator proposes a transfer to another active administrator, who accepts it with five-minute strong authentication within seven days (an engineering choice mirroring invitation validity); one pending transfer per company, cancel/decline, expiry, and visibility only to the two parties. Each change writes one audit event; the reviewed migration 20261018030000_roles_and_responsibility_transfer adds the transfer table, and integration tests cover IA-04 (bypass, last administrator, incomplete transfer). The panel shows grants, adds/revokes them, proposes transfers and shows pending transfers to their parties; a browser journey enrolls the successor's OTP and accepts responsibility through the real session. Frozen install and full local pnpm validate passed: 116 API tests, 67 web unit tests, 23 browser component tests and 24 E2E journeys. Invitations and durable email delivery, branch-manager delegation of operator grants and custom profiles remain coordinated with PJ-24. PH-15–PH-17 gate real environments. 2026-10-18: the owner approved the D-13 invitation and email delivery design and ADR-0026 under PH-21 (PJ-30); invitation implementation (including branch managers inviting operators) has started. Invitations and durable email (2026-10-18): a mail API module (PostgreSQL outbox in the producer's transaction, in-process dispatcher with SKIP LOCKED leases, eight attempts over about 22 hours, sealed credentials erased at the final state, 30-day purge, TELUNI_MAIL_* settings and nodemailer 10.1.2) and an invitations module (create, list, resend, revoke, preview, accept; hashed 256-bit credentials in a URL fragment; acceptance only by the matching verified identity with revalidation; active/suspended/removed membership cases with a partial uniqueness rule; abuse limits; 90-day address tombstones) with reviewed migrations 20261018040000_mail_outbox and 20261018050000_company_invitations, a panel Invitations view and acceptance page, and a journey that reads the invitation from Mailpit and accepts it. Frozen install and full local pnpm validate passed: 148 API tests, 67 web unit tests, 28 browser component tests and 24 E2E journeys. Branch-scoped audit (2026-10-19): strongly authenticated branch managers read the change history of their own branches only, meaning events that concern at least one branch and no branch outside their grants; company-level events stay with administrators and operators still have no audit access. The reviewed migration 20261019020000_branch_audit_scope adds the append-only organization_audit_event_branches table with composite references and backfills existing events from branch targets and grant/invitation branch scopes; the branch predicate runs before ordering and the limit, and audit cursors bind the caller's branch scope. The panel offers the history view to managers with branch-specific copy. Checks run locally: frozen install, format, lint, typecheck, architecture, documentation, agent instructions, release history, provenance, generated references, build and smoke passed; 129 API tests (organizations integration, invitations and domain suites against real PostgreSQL), 67 web unit tests, 34 browser component tests and the 16 E2E journeys that do not need Keycloak passed. Attempt 2 passed all 323 API, 72 web unit and 92 browser tests, plus build and smoke, but exhausted the 35-minute job budget after about 28 minutes preparing system packages through the Azure Ubuntu mirror; E2E had started and did not complete.

The corrective increment keeps that job budget and every test assertion: CI uses the Ubuntu archive over HTTPS with bounded package-network retries/timeouts, reuses Playwright's refreshed package index for FFmpeg, and pre-pulls the job's explicit Testcontainers host-port helper image before parallel fixtures. The mail integration test compares the deadline with a database statement timestamp cast to the same millisecond precision as next_attempt_at; storage can round a deadline upward by half a millisecond, so comparing it to an unrounded clock produced a false upper-bound failure. Runtime retry timing, migrations and permissions are unchanged. The focused mail integration/domain run passed all 11 tests. The initial correction at 79cf54c did not cover the hosted runner's /etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt indirection: run 39969449887 again exhausted the job budget downloading packages. The follow-up covers both direct sources and that mirror list. A disposable Ubuntu probe of the workflow block verifies both source formats, retains the security mirror and signing key, and enforces the package-network options. Full qualification remains pending the follow-up head's own CI result; earlier attempts are diagnostic evidence only. The latest full local gate reached the API suite and reported 293 passed, 13 failed and 17 skipped: existing Windows image-path/media-reserve failures and one transport timeout; the focused mail tests remain green.

The follow-up at 0125c1d qualified the prerequisite corrections in run 39985390489: package downloads took seconds, all 323 API, 72 unit and 92 browser tests passed, as did build, smoke, Player, Deployment rehearsal and Dependency review. Full E2E reached 41 passed and one failed: the media journey's substring locator for “logo” also matched the newly persistent “Catálogos” sidebar link. Both media reopen actions now require the exact accessible name, preserving the original preview/archive/trash/restore assertions. The next head must pass its own complete gate.

Device workflow interface increment

On 2026-10-24 the owner requested autonomous development after testing the upgraded product. Work continues from merged Orion upgrade 6ab489c on codex/device-workflow-interface. This PJ-41 increment adopts the existing shared Button and TextField contracts in screen pairing, configuration, move, unlink and manual-reset actions. Domain-specific messages, request bodies, capability checks, versions, strong-authentication prompts and confirmation gates stay in the device feature; native selects and confirmation checkboxes remain native. No new UI abstraction, provider, database migration or permission is introduced.

Screen lists use themed cards; long device, branch and reported-model values wrap, and the unlink confirmation retains a native-sized checkbox instead of inheriting the text-input width. An unknown pairing outcome blocks another submission, including implicit form submission, until the person explicitly reloads and checks the list. A failed destination lookup exposes a read error and explicit reload rather than silently hiding the move action or offering cached destinations; truncated choices retain their existing warning. Pending actions expose busy state and disable activation. Existing shared ErrorNotice wording is not substituted for the feature's localized read/write semantics.

Focused qualification includes eleven device component tests, covering pending/lost-response reconciliation without repeated writes and destination-lookup recovery, and four presentation E2E journeys. The journeys cover real browser rendering, keyboard operation, hints, long values, confirmation, revoked/reset states, light/dark themes and desktop/320-pixel layouts with automated accessibility checks and screenshots; representative desktop/light and mobile/dark screenshots were visually reviewed. Existing real-provider pairing/check-in/erasure journeys remain the integration gate. Full repository validation and current-head CI remain required and are recorded in the increment's PR. Other modules' detailed states, final visual refinement and provider appearance remain pending under PJ-41; this increment does not complete the entire interface task.

Local development MFA option

Superseded on 2026-10-28 by optional two-step verification; the setting below was removed.

On 2026-10-24 the owner requested optional two-step verification for development while testing the local panel. This PJ-24 increment adds the server-only TELUNI_DEV_MFA_MODE setting, default required, with a guarded optional mode for development on loopback only. The identity design owns the exception's semantics; setup owned activation and reversal. The session boundary still authenticates and checks CSRF, expiry and revocation, then projects local effective assurance without persisting a false MFA event. The panel labels the exception explicitly. No schema, provider flow, production permission, real-environment gate or procurement changes. Configuration, real-Keycloak/PostgreSQL and browser tests cover the exception and restoration of required enforcement. Frozen install and full local VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-24: 334 API tests, 73 web unit tests, 98 browser component tests and 49 E2E journeys. The first default-worker gate timed out at five seconds in the unchanged price-publication integration test; all nine publication tests passed in isolation, and the complete gate passed sequentially without changing test limits or assertions. Password-only login and existing company access were also verified in the running local environment. No remote CI result is claimed.

Optional two-step verification

On 2026-10-28 the owner revised P12/P14 (PH-20 follow-up): two-step verification is optional for every company user, administrators and branch managers included; each person enables or disables it; a person who enabled it gives the code at every sign-in; Teluni suggests it after the first sign-in without requiring it; sensitive operations ask for the password again (plus the code when enabled) within five minutes; disabling asks for the password and current code. This PJ-24 increment replaces the teluni-browser-v1 step-up flow with teluni-browser-v2 (conditional OTP), adds the enable/disable account actions, GET /auth/two-step and the /welcome/two-step suggestion, replaces requireStrongAuthentication/STRONG_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED with requireRecentAuthentication, removes the strong-authentication requirement from organization grants and the capabilitiesAfterStrongAuthentication access field, and removes TELUNI_DEV_MFA_MODE. The human_sessions.strong_authenticated_at and oidc_login_attempts.requested_assurance columns are no longer written or read; the reviewed contract migration 20261028000000_retire_strong_authentication_columns drops them, to be applied only after no older API that writes them is running (no durable environment exists yet, and the dropped ephemeral values are not recoverable). The identity design and policies own the behavior. Recovery codes and passkeys remain pending, so losing an enabled authenticator needs assisted recovery. Local validation on 2026-10-28, run as the separate pnpm validate steps: format, lint, typecheck, architecture, documentation, agent-instruction, environment-example, deployment, release, Orion, reference and portal checks; 349 API tests with real Keycloak 26.8.1 and PostgreSQL (two assertions of the old rule adjusted and rerun in their files); 75 web unit and 119 browser component tests; the build and smoke; and all 50 end-to-end journeys (the new identity journey failed once on a hidden-field selector, was fixed, and its whole file then passed). No remote CI result is claimed.

Full-width companies page and theme switch

On 2026-10-28 the owner asked for less empty space on /companies at desktop resolutions, with the DataSet occupying most of the page, for the top header ("Seu espaço de trabalho" and the theme selector) to be removed and for a simpler sun/moon theme switch at the bottom of the sidebar. The desktop shell has no top header; narrow screens keep a bar with only the menu button. The switch (role="switch", “Tema escuro”) sits beside the collapse control and stays usable when the sidebar is collapsed; it follows the system until used, and choosing a theme no longer offers returning to System. The companies page removes the content width limit and, from 761 px, fills the viewport height with the grid scrolling inside the dataset frame; other pages keep their widths. A pre-existing narrow-screen defect that centered short pages vertically below the menu bar was fixed. Browser component tests, the shell, company-navigation, device-interface, screens and companies E2E journeys passed locally; no remote CI result is claimed.

DataSet filter modal

On 2026-10-28 the owner asked for a Filter option in the DataSet, right of Refresh, opening a modal with the dataset's filters and shown only on datasets that have filters, then for it to show only its icon. The optional filters prop (active count and a render function for the caller's fields) adds an icon-only action whose accessible name and tooltip include the active count, also shown as a badge, and a native modal dialog that keeps focus inside, closes with Escape, its close button or a backdrop click and returns focus to the action. The screens page moved its server-side branch and status filters into the modal with Apply and Clear. Component metadata, browser component tests and the screens test were updated.

Branches and screens as datasets

On 2026-10-28 the owner asked for the branches and screens lists to use the DataSet component. The company page's branches view and /companies/$companyId/screens now use it with the full-workspace layout of the companies page (shared dataset-panel/dataset-region styles). Branches show name, status and time zone; the form creates a branch or renames and archives the selected one, keeping the version observed when editing started. Screens show name, branch, status with erasure, last check-in and synchronization under the existing server-side branch and status filters; adding a record opens pairing, and the form shows a screen summary linking to the screen page, where configuration, moving, unlinking and history stay. Mode and record live in the route search. When there is no record yet, a manager starts on the form, pinned in the URL so it survives the record it adds; both forms gained a Cancel action. Browser component tests and the affected E2E journeys were updated.

Collapsible sidebar increment

On 2026-10-26 the owner requested visual refinements, starting with a collapsible left sidebar. On desktop widths, a localized “Recolher menu”/“Expandir menu” control at the foot of the sidebar narrows it to a brand mark and navigation icons. Link and button labels remain in the accessibility tree, the company context label and switch link are hidden while collapsed, and every product and portal entry now carries an icon. Only teluni.sidebar=collapsed is stored, with the same tab synchronization and storage-denial fallback as the theme; expanding removes the key. The mobile menu ignores the stored layout. No route, permission or API behavior changes. A shell E2E journey covers collapse, reload persistence, navigation, both themes with axe scans, and the mobile fallback.

Companies dataset increment

On 2026-10-26 the owner asked for a reusable record component similar to Sankhya's sk-dataset and for its use on the companies page. The shared, presentation-only DataSet in apps/web/src/dataset.tsx (exported through components.tsx, with catalog metadata and a synthetic example) provides a toolbar to switch between grid and form modes, add, move to the previous or next record, duplicate and refresh, a grid with labeled radio selection (double-click opens the form), and an optional delete action. Features keep records, selection, mode, API calls, permissions and drafts; an omitted handler disables its action.

The companies page keeps its mode, selected record and duplication source in validated URL search parameters next to the existing cursor. The form edits settings through the existing versioned PATCH /companies/{companyId} with step-up and read-only states, creates companies with the existing idempotent request and still opens the new company's workspace afterwards, and duplication pre-fills a new company from the selected one's name, time zone and language. A person with no company lands directly on the new-company form. Moving between records, switching mode and refreshing are disabled while the form has unsaved changes. The company workspace's settings view reuses the same fields. Delete is not offered: the API has no company deletion, and adding it needs its own design for retention, members, devices, media and audit before any endpoint exists. Navigation moves within the current page; the existing cursor links still change pages. Browser component tests cover the component and the URL-owned companies dataset; the companies E2E journey covers selection, form mode, draft cancellation, duplication, axe scans and narrow-width overflow.

Companies dataset grid increment

On 2026-10-27 the owner asked for configurable multiple selection in DataSet (not offered on the companies page), selection shown only by a light color instead of a radio, subtle lines between header and body cells, resizable columns, sorting by clicking a header, a header options icon on hover with "Ordem Crescente", "Ordem Decrescente" and "Filtrar", and a value filter with search, select-all and one or more values. The grid and the filter list had to stay fast with very many rows, using the best available technology and reusing components.

ADR-0034 selects headless TanStack Table v9 and TanStack Virtual v3. A new shared DataGrid in apps/web/src/data-grid.tsx renders only the rows in view with ARIA grid roles, row counts and indexes; rows form one tab stop with arrow, Page, Home/End, Enter and Space keys, and multiple adds Ctrl/⌘ and Shift selection and Ctrl/⌘+A. Headers sort on click, expose aria-sort, show a filter icon while filtered, and resize by dragging, double-click reset or arrow keys on a labeled separator. The filter lists each column's values under the other columns' filters; with a search, Apply keeps only the chosen values found, and choosing every value removes the filter. A live status shows shown, total and selected counts, and a filter that leaves no row offers Clear filters. DataSet composes it, keeps sorting, filters and widths while switching to the form, and derives previous/next from the order shown, so onPrevious, onNext and rowName were removed.

New shared components, each with catalog metadata and a live example: Checkbox (native input with a mixed state), Popover (native popover attribute in the top layer, anchored, focus return), Menu (labeled trigger and keyboard menu), MultiSelectList (virtualized, accent-insensitive search, select-all, listbox with active descendant) and DataGrid. Button, TextField and Checkbox moved to controls.tsx so composed components can use them without an import cycle; components.tsx still exports them. The --ui-color-divider token maps to Teluni's border color. The companies page uses single selection with sortable, filterable name and access columns; sorting and filtering cover the loaded page, and server-side processing is not provided. No API, schema or permission changes.

The owner then asked for exports to Excel and PDF, leaving other formats to the agent. ADR-0035 adds Excel (.xlsx), CSV and PDF, offered only where a screen passes exportName: an Exportar menu in the DataSet toolbar or the DataGrid footer saves the rows shown, in their order and with their filters, and the columns that have a value. Excel keeps numbers numeric with a bold, frozen header and the widths shown; CSV is UTF-8 with a byte order mark, ; separators and decimal commas in Portuguese, and guards text that spreadsheets would run as formulas; PDF is A4 with a title, generation time, record count and page numbers. write-excel-file, jsPDF and jspdf-autotable load only when someone exports; core-js's install script, an optional jsPDF dependency, stays disabled. The companies page exports as "Empresas". Unit tests cover the CSV rules and a browser test saves all three formats from a sorted grid.

Local validation on 2026-10-27 on Windows: format, lint, type, architecture, documentation and reference checks passed; web unit (75) and browser component tests (120) passed; the build, bundle checks and API smoke passed; 35 end-to-end journeys passed, including the shell, company navigation and portal journeys. Failures outside this change, in files it does not touch: deployment:test joins two absolute Windows paths; 14 API tests (media processing, the Keycloak image and integration cases that create media) failed; and the 7 journeys that start the local API stack, including the companies journey with its new export step, stopped when the API rejected its configuration at startup, with 8 dependent journeys not run. The companies dataset is covered by browser tests against a simulated API. No remote CI result is claimed.

Phase sequence and exit criteria

These phases are an initial roadmap, not permission to implement. Dependencies can be refined using pilot evidence without deleting unresolved work. No dates, staffing, price or capacity commitments are inferred from the brief.

Phase Scope and task owners Exit criteria / current position
1 — Project foundation Derivation/repository gate (PJ-01); product identity/requirements/documentation (PJ-02/PJ-04); entity/module and architecture review (PJ-07); deployment strategy (PJ-13 planning) Product brief and traceable MVP acceptance documented; architecture directions accepted; detailed design reviewed before dependent slices; pilot hardware/identity/operating inputs recorded. Documentation alone does not complete the phase.
2 — Initial operational release Human identity/scoped access (PJ-24) and tenant-safe first slice (PJ-03); devices (PJ-08); media (PJ-09); programming (PJ-10); publication/sync/monitoring (PJ-11); Android offline player (PJ-12); freeform hybrid presentation (PJ-20); configurable data catalogs (PJ-21); basic commercial access (PJ-27); deploy/recover (PJ-13); Connected Tiles interface alignment (PJ-41); integrated acceptance (PJ-14) Full release journey passes, including regional schedules, multiple-video/audio rendering, generic catalogs/data bindings, cross-tenant denial, CP-01–CP-12 commercial admission/expiry/quota cases, real hardware/power/network tests, restore/migration rehearsal and nontechnical pilot observation. Actual customer/cost/support/fiscal readiness remains PH-18/PH-19 at its applicable milestone. The owner prioritizes approved product capability/quality over reducing scope to an MVP label. Record measurements and residual risk; planning does not prove release readiness.
3 — Professional features PJ-15, reprioritized after pilot Separate approved requirements and evidence for each selected feature; not all items must be delivered as one release.
4 — Commercial expansion PJ-16, based on demand and sustainable operation Separate approved scope, compatibility/security/cost review and demonstrated customer need for each expansion.

Professional and expansion backlog

All items here are future and require separate scope review. The approved initial release already includes configurable catalogs, textual import/export, freeform regional presentation, version protection and monitoring; extensions must not hide those requirements.

Phase / area Candidate scope Important design dependency
3 — Presentation extensions Richer widgets such as QR codes, clocks/external information and personalization beyond the approved freeform authoring model FR-10/PJ-20 already include freeform composition, regional schedules and multiple videos. Versioning and validated textual copy/import/export are already initial requirements; richer widgets and eventual AI authorship require separate approval. Do not depend only on flattened images
3 — Catalog extensions Further specialized external/transactional catalog workflows beyond configurable typed collections and published data views FR-11/PJ-21 already cover custom fields, product/weekly-agenda configurations, scoped monetary overrides and automatic price publication. This does not approve an ERP/POS engine
3 — Campaigns Promotional periods, priorities, automatic start/end, scheduling and publication history Deterministic conflicts/expiry and version semantics, extending the MVP playlist schedule
3 — Professional operation Advanced monitoring, change history and operator-directed version recovery Version retention and validity, privacy and audit; MVP last-valid recovery already required
4 — Integrations Public documented APIs, ERP/POS price/product updates, webhooks, file imports and dynamic sources Scoped machine identities, versioned OpenAPI documentation available to partners, idempotency/replay and rate limits
4 — Enterprise fleets Advanced fleet organization and rollout controls, playback reports, operational alerts and support tools Basic persistent-group assignment across branches of the same company is MVP scope under FR-05; deeper fleet features require measured scale, safe support access and minimized reporting data
4 — Commercial features Further plan segmentation, subscription/payment automation, annual/international/partner offers, advanced personalization and white-label; the initial single-plan manual entitlement flow is already PJ-27 Validated pricing/limits/support/cancellation/tax and provider costs; no gateway dependency for MVP
4 — Players Web player, other Smart TVs, computers/dedicated devices; possible synchronized screens Platform-specific capability/update tests and feasibility/clock/network evidence before synchronized-playback promises
4 — AI Assisted artwork, campaign suggestions, advertising text and layout adaptation Explicit budgets, privacy/IP review, operator approval and portability; paid inference must not gate core signage
4 — Infrastructure VPS/cloud, optional S3-compatible storage and capacity expansion Measured bottlenecks/revenue or operating needs; preserve tested migration and recovery rather than adding microservices by default

Progress and plan changes

Current task statuses own progress. Git preserves detailed editing history. Do not remove unresolved tasks or activation conditions when consolidating completed work.
